# Daily Log Summary — 2026-05-10

## Executive summary
- Day focused on observability, auditability, and recovery readiness while keeping changes local, read-only where possible, and low-complexity.
- Implemented MVP dashboard metrics for token efficiency, observe-only stability, and tools/plugins inventory.
- Created stricter governance for Internet access, fortnightly audits, and operational backups/recovery.

## Important events
- Added “tokens per useful task” MVP using local JSONL metrics and estimated `session_status` snapshots; no external APIs or cost.
- Added observe-only stability MVP with score, uptime, resource usage, token-rate estimate, errors, loops, restarts, and anomalous consumption.
- Audited tools/plugins read-only: 92 plugins discovered, 67 loaded, 25 disabled, plugin doctor clean, 7 eligible skills, 3 active crons.
- Created protocol documents for Internet access, fortnightly core/general audits, and backups/recovery.
- Enabled lightweight operational/historical backup automation for non-sensitive B/C material; first backup verified OK.

## Errors / failures
- The token-usage alert initially had a visibility issue from an isolated session; it was corrected to target the current session.
- Stability metrics reported 0 critical errors, 0 loops detected, and 0 confirmed gateway restarts. Four apparent errors were classified as false positives from templates/reports.

## Correct actions / good decisions
- Kept new observability in observation-only mode: no automatic restarts, no tool freezing, no external services.
- Preserved the principle “Orden, rigor y seguridad”: order first, measure next, automate only what is safe.
- Recommended that any external dashboard access start as static/read-only and avoid exposing OpenClaw or internal tools.
- Chose restore capability as the real backup objective, including verification, manifests/checksums, retention, and isolated restore testing.
